### Gideon’s Short-Lived Revival
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/gideons-short-lived-revival
Passage: Judges 8:27
Points:
- Despite winning great victories and tearing down pagan altars, Gideon and Israel quickly lapsed into idolatry.
- Gideon outwardly refused the crown with pious words, yet gave his son a royal name implying kingship.
- By fashioning a golden ephod out of Midianite plunder, Gideon led his family and nation into spiritual ruin.
- Faithful service does not prevent believers from succumbing to compromise later in life.
- Christians must remain watchful and grounded in Scripture to avoid finishing poorly.

### The Child Who Raised an Army
Author: Tod Twist
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/the-child-that-raised-an-army.html
Passage: Judges 8:22-35
Points:
- Gideon publicly turned down the kingship, yet named his son Abimelech, meaning "my father is king."
- Lingering insecurities over feeling weak drove Gideon toward self-promotion, retaliation, and human control.
- Setting up a sacred ephod in his hometown centralized worship around himself and snared the nation.
- The earthly power Gideon attempted to secure was ultimately dismantled through his son's destructive reign.
- God works by reducing human strength so believers rely on His power rather than their own.
